name: Shakespeare Imitation Game (SIG)
description: This record contains two linked working papers defining and operationalising the Shakespeare Imitation Game (SIG), a proposed benchmark for reciprocal embodied artificial intelligence. The main paper, The Shakespeare Imitation Game: A Benchmark for Reciprocal Embodied Artificial Intelligence, develops the benchmark methodology. SIG asks whether an autonomous embodied system can sustain reciprocal, context-sensitive dramatic interaction when a professional human scene partner introduces an unannounced, character-relevant change. Rather than testing script recitation, visual human-likeness or theatrical mimicry, the benchmark evaluates whether the autonomous performer remains interpretively coherent, responds meaningfully to its partner, and in turn causes that partner to change. The methodology uses three calibration anchors: live human-human performance, a professional Shakespearean actor teleoperating the test robot, and an autonomous embodied artificial intelligence controlling the same robot. This separates embodiment/interface loss from the remaining autonomy gap. A platform-specific Embodiment Transmission Ceiling prevents limitations of the robotic body or teleoperation interface from being misclassified as failures of artificial intelligence. The benchmark further uses interpretively discriminating perturbations, blinded controller assignment, partner-side measures of reciprocal responsiveness and compensatory effort, and a pre-registered non-inferiority framework.
